newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market calm and stable, ignoring Buba.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market calm and stable, ignoring Buba.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were mostly glued to Wednesday's levels in slow trade on Thursday, ignoring several Bundesbank announcements.

"The Buba's decision to leave its (main interest) rates unchanged did not surprise the market, and although their M3 growth target for the next two years does seem rather low to me, it does not matter much to us," one dealer said, adding that the actual M3 figures would be carefully watched next year.
"It's the results that count, not the targets," he said.
The Buba set its M3 growth target for 1997 and 1998 at 3.5 to 6.5 percent, bringing it down from the current four to seven percent, which has been continuously surpassed this year.
It also announced it kept its main discount, lombard and repo rates unchanged, as expected by market players.
Trade was again slow due to the end-of-year effect.
"The (money) market will lay backwards till January," one dealer said.
He said most activity was concentrated in call money and up to the end of December. Overnight money was quoted between 2.81 and 2.94 around 1400 GMT.
One to three month deposits were quoted slightly higher than yesterday (3.02-3.10), but were not very active, dealers said.
"There are some parties keen on buying over the year-end, but no sellers. The rates for these deposits are below what I consider as realistic," one dealer said.
The guilder was quoted at 112.240 per 100 marks, virtually unchanged from yesterday (112.235).
